profile.address: Campus Universitario de Espinardo, Murcia, Spain
profile.reading:
This is KIO Networks España's data center on the University of Murcia's Espinardo campus in Murcia, Spain, the company's only operating site in the country while a second building, in Paterna near Valencia, was still under construction as of late 2024. Spanish press covering the 2024 change of ownership describe a computer room of 172 square meters built to hold equipment rated at 193 kilowatts, set on seismic resistant pedestals, backed by two redundant 600 kVA uninterruptible power supplies whose batteries are continuously monitored through a SCADA system, and supported by two 1,200 kilowatt diesel generators, a combined nameplate of about 2.4 megawatts of standby generation, reported to run the facility for roughly four days on stored diesel. Both the electrical and cooling systems are described as running in a 2N high availability configuration. Separately, a 2017 Spanish language Data Center Dynamics report on the same Murcia facility described it as Tier IV certified under the Uptime Institute framework, with roughly 2,500 square meters of overall constructed area, and reported that the site was entering Spain's first CEEDA energy efficiency certification process that year, a program administered by DCD to assess operational management, mechanical, electrical, IT infrastructure, and deployment efficiency, following three earlier CEEDA certifications KIO had already obtained at facilities in Mexico. The 2,500 square meter figure describes the building as a whole, while the 172 square meter and 193 kilowatt figures describe the technical computer room specifically. Neither source available to this registry explicitly labeled the 193 kilowatt figure as IT load or critical load, so it is reported here as a room level power rating rather than asserted as a verified IT capacity number.

KIO Networks España began as a joint venture in which Spanish retail group El Corte Inglés held a 50 percent stake alongside Mexican data center operator KIO Networks. El Corte Inglés completed a buyout of the remaining 50 percent on October 1, 2024, a transaction recorded with Spain's Commercial Registry that made the retailer sole owner of the Spanish subsidiary. The deal dissolved the prior board, which had been chaired by Federico Jimeno Cuéllar, and put day to day oversight under Jaime de la Hera Cremades alongside Javier Felipe Egea Caballero, El Corte Inglés' director of strategy, corporate development and holdings, reporting under company president Marta Álvarez. Spanish business press framed the acquisition as El Corte Inglés' entry into managing data center capacity for outside clients rather than only for its own retail IT needs, and multiple outlets noted the transaction price was not disclosed.

The Paterna facility near Valencia, described at the time of the Murcia buyout coverage as nearing completion and due to open in 2025, is reported elsewhere as roughly 1,000 square meters of Tier IV certified IT room space with about 2.4 megawatts of power, of which about 1 megawatt is allocated to servers, built at a stated investment exceeding 50 million euros and expected to create around 70 direct jobs, using a CO2 based cooling system chosen partly to limit water use. Those Paterna numbers describe that separate, newer building and should not be read as describing the Espinardo site in Murcia that this record covers. The Mexican KIO Networks brand behind the original 50 percent stake in the Spanish venture no longer lists Spain among the countries covered on its own current data center portfolio pages, consistent with El Corte Inglés having taken full, independent ownership of the Spanish operation and its two buildings.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-06. Prior profile version cited datacentermap.com, dcpulse.com, and Wikipedia (El Corte Ingles article) in its sources array; datacentermap.com and Wikipedia are excluded under current house rules so the entry was redone from allowed sources. Fresh research used a 2017 DCD Spanish-language article on the CEEDA certification (Tier IV, ~2500 sqm building), murciaeconomia.com local coverage of the same 2017 story, murciaplaza.com's 2024 report on the El Corte Ingles full buyout (172 sqm / 193 kW room, UPS/generator specs), theobjective.com and valenciaplaza.com coverage of the same 2024 transaction and the separate, not-yet-opened Paterna (Valencia) building. Corrected: prior profile's it_capacity_mw of 0.193 has been removed because no source explicitly labels the 193 kW figure as IT or critical load; it is room-level power only, now described as such in prose. Corrected: prior profile implied "a second, larger KIO facility under development in Valencia" without giving it a name or numbers; sourced version now identifies it specifically as Paterna, with its own explicitly-scoped 2.4 MW / 1 MW-to-servers / 1000 sqm figures, kept clearly separated from the Murcia figures per the house power-field rule. Checked and rejected as citations: datacentermap.com (address "Calle Santiago Navarro 8" claim, not corroborated elsewhere and therefore also not used), dcpulse.com, Wikipedia. Could not verify: a specific street address for the Murcia building (only "Espinardo campus" is corroborated across allowed sources).
